questions.q: Why does response speed matter for customer retention?
questions.a: A quick reply tells guests they matter and that someone is acting on their experience. Slow or impersonal responses feel like a brush-off, and unhappy guests are quick to take their business elsewhere. Handled fast and personally, a complaint can even leave a guest more likely to return than if nothing had gone wrong.

questions.q: How quickly should a restaurant respond to a negative review?
questions.a: Aim to respond within 24 hours, and sooner for serious complaints. The longer a review sits, the less your reply matters to the guest and to people reading it later. Mapping your current response times by location is a good first step, since some stores may be far behind others.

questions.q: Who should respond to customer feedback in a multi-location restaurant brand?
questions.a: Store managers are usually best placed to respond, because guests want action where the experience happened. Give them real-time access to feedback, brand-approved reply guidelines and the authority to respond publicly to reviews and privately to surveys. Keep a clear path to escalate serious issues to regional or corporate teams.

questions.q: How can store teams respond quickly without getting overwhelmed?
questions.a: A central hub that routes feedback by location, issue type and urgency keeps the workload manageable. AI-suggested replies and mobile tools let managers answer from their phones in minutes, while escalation workflows send serious complaints to the right department. Momos brings these pieces together on one platform so even non-technical staff can respond with confidence.

questions.q: How do I measure whether faster feedback responses are working?
questions.a: Track outcomes alongside reply counts. Look at how response speed relates to return visits, revised reviews, loyalty sign-ups and issues resolved at each store. Closed-loop reporting that connects replies to guest behavior shows which locations and habits are paying off.
